description: We're a team searching for education, and upgrade coding skills
summary:
Pulse! is a crew health monitoring simulator played as a space crew, the ship on a long duration mission. It runs in the browser and in VR or mixed reality on Meta Quest. It continuously tracks each astronaut's health, stress, sleep, morale and trust, together with the ship's environment (life support, air quality, food, medicine). When indicators cross risk thresholds, the system raises warnings. Before every decision it shows the probability of success and its causes. The user can act on the warnings by ordering rest, infirmary care or free time. Ignoring the signs has consequences that build over time.

The challenge asks for tools that help astronauts spot and act on changes in their own health far from Earth. Pulse! makes that cycle of gathering, evaluating and acting tangible, and it trains the habit that keeps crews alive on long missions.
details:
What it does / how it works

Pulse! puts the user in the role of N0VA-7, the onboard AI responsible for a five-person crew on a long-duration mission. Every crew member has live health indicators: health, stress, sleep, morale and trust. The ship has its own environmental indicators: life support, power, hull, food and medicine. The app runs a continuous cycle:

- Gather: indicators change in real time with workload, rest, events and the closed environment. One example is saturated air filters raising CO₂.

- Evaluate: when someone crosses a risk threshold (high stress, sleep deprivation, low health), the system flags it. Before any assignment it shows the probability of success and the factors behind it.

- Act: the user can order rest, infirmary care, free time or a return to duty, or assign tasks and missions. Overriding a warning has consequences. Trust drops, and repeated overrides leave lasting resentment.

Every decision is recorded in a mission log. The game has no fixed ending: the crew must survive as long as possible while difficulty increases.

Benefits and intended impact

It turns abstract health monitoring into a habit: notice early signs, understand their causes, and act before they become a crisis. It shows that physical health, mental health and the environment are linked, and that pushing an exhausted crew costs more later. It can serve as a training and awareness tool for self-monitoring on isolated missions, and as an engaging way to teach the public about crew health in space.

Tools and technology

- TypeScript, React 19, Vite, Zustand, Zod and React Router

- 3D and VR: Three.js, React Three Fiber, drei and WebXR (@react-three/xr)

- Testing: Vitest and Playwright

- Hardware: Meta Quest 3, with VR and mixed-reality (passthrough) support. Also runs in any desktop browser.

- All 3D textures and sound effects are generated in code, so there is nothing heavy to download. Progress is saved locally.

Creativity

Instead of a dashboard, pulse makes health monitoring an experience. In VR, the ship appears as a holographic command table surrounded by the crew's faces and task panels. Players can walk through the ship at life size or sit in the cockpit while stars streak past at warp, which is unlocked only when no tasks are pending. The user is not a single astronaut but the AI that watches over everyone, which shows why someone, or something, must always be paying attention.

Factors we considered

- Clarity: every warning explains its cause.

- Comfort in VR: fade transitions instead of moving the player, panels within arm's reach, and a fixed cabin frame during warp to reduce motion sickness.

- Accessibility: reduced-motion option, works with mouse, controllers or hand tracking.

- Performance: runs on a standalone headset, even over a slow network.

- Honesty: we model behavioral and general health indicators rather than claiming clinical simulation of radiation or bone loss.
